==== Page 1 ====
Incremental Hybrid Retrieval for Agentic Knowledge
Workflows
Collection-owned storage, reusable indexes, and source-bound answer verification
Draft 0.9 — 15 November 2026
Evidence cutoff: 15 November 2026
Abstract
We describe a collection-local knowledge engine for chang-
ing document corpora and agentic workflows. Vec-
tor shards, text derivatives and relational metadata
form a revision-bound derived generation; original as-
sets commit separately, so source changes invalidate
stale passages before refresh. Exact chunk/window
hashes reduce repeated embedding and extraction
work. Document routes separate local parsing, optional
OCR/transcription, inferred visual descriptions and na-
tive multimodal embedding. Encrypted storage is the
default; an explicit clear portable format instead pro-
vides checksums without confidentiality or publisher au-
thentication. A self-contained directory transfers its
generation-bound model contract while local grants and
provider consent remain separate. Federation composes
bounded ranks and qualified graph records without merg-
ing vector spaces or stores. Agents inspect paginated
sources and exact evidence receipts. Optional answer
review validates quotations and claim spans, revises once
and rechecks before covered chat paths publish a hash-
bound answer/report. Encrypted-storage measurements
and controlled portability, retrieval and source-support
fixtures exercise the mechanisms without establishing
general accuracy or factual truth. Keywords: Hybrid
retrieval; Incremental indexing; Encrypted collections;
Agent tool contracts; Evidence provenance; Answer veri-
fication.
Draft 0.9. This report describes implemented mecha-
nisms and bounded experiments, with software behavior
distinguished from empirical quality estimates. Findings
retain the specific scope described in Section 9.
1
Problem and relationship to
prior work
A personal or team knowledge engine must manage a
changing corpus, rather than only produce a top-K vec-
tor result. Exact project identifiers may matter more
than paraphrase similarity; a question about every client
requires enumeration; replacing a file must invalidate
stale evidence; and a protected document must remain
protected after OCR, indexing and citation. These re-
quirements motivate a software architecture in which
retrieval, source lifecycle and access authority are ex-
plicit contracts.
BM25 supplies a lexical lane for exact terms, while
dense vectors support semantic matching. Reciprocal-
rank fusion (RRF) combines ordered candidates without
assuming comparable score magnitudes. This is a prac-
tical default across independently configured collections,
although hybrid-fusion research shows that tuned score
combinations can outperform RRF on particular data.
The engine therefore treats fusion as a replaceable policy,
not a universal optimum. [1] [2] [3]
LightRAG and GraphRAG motivate connecting tex-
tual retrieval with extracted entities and relationships.
The present design adopts source-linked metadata but
avoids mandatory corpus-wide community-report regen-
eration during ordinary updates. Each document owns
its derived entities, relations and summaries; a bounded
graph view is an inspection interface over those records.
Graph edges do not automatically become another rank-
ing lane. Recent work on provenance-aware deletion
likewise reinforces document ownership as a lifecycle con-
cern, while iterative retrieval research motivates exposing
several small inspection tools rather than one opaque
retrieval call. [4] [5] [6] [7]
RankGPT and RankLLM provide the basis for op-
tional listwise LLM reranking over a bounded candidate
set. ALCE, RAGChecker and RAGBench motivate sep-
arating retrieval quality, attribution and answer sup-
port. Here these ideas are composed through local inter-
faces: an extractor writes anchored metadata, a reranker
changes order, and a verifier assesses claims against sup-
plied evidence. Their responsibilities and data exposure
remain separate. [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]
2
Components and
persistent
contracts
The collection is the unit of ownership, configuration,
storage policy and authorization. A storage adapter
supplies immutable assets and logical aliases; the index-
ing coordinator supplies source enumeration, revision
discovery, parsing and model calls. Encryption is the
default storage envelope, with an explicitly selected clear
directory format for public data. Portable engines oper-
ate through these ports, so the same vector, metadata
and verification logic can run in desktop and mobile
hosts without a graph server or Python service. Figure
1 summarizes the data paths.

representation; native media can bypass text derivation. A compatible embedding adapter is required for the selected modality.
The enclosure denotes collection ownership, not a transaction over originals and derived data: sources commit before the
separate derived-generation pointer. The query encoder is omitted for clarity: hybrid search also embeds the query in the
collection's own space. Metadata expansion leads to source inspection, not directly into RRF.

The vector index records a non-secret embedding-space
identity covering provider type, endpoint, model, dimen-
sions, transport and any declared model revision. A space
mismatch fails before a query is sent; explicit rebuilding
is required. Credentials are excluded, so rotating a key
alone does not invalidate stored vectors. In-flight author-
ity checks still detect changed credentials or provider
settings. This distinction prevents both accidental reuse
across endpoints and unnecessary re-embedding after
routine key rotation.
New vector shards use an FP32 little-endian payload
encoded as base64 inside the selected storage envelope,
authenticated and encrypted by default. The reader
accepts packed records and legacy numeric arrays, in-
cluding mixed collections. With valid space bindings,
the codec change alone requires no new inference for
unchanged records. Runtime feature detection uses na-
tive byte-array base64 conversion where available and an
atob/btoa fallback elsewhere; validation checks canonical
padding, dimensions and finite values while avoiding an
unnecessary second array copy. FP32 rounds JavaScript
numeric values; a controlled fixture kept cosine-score
deviation below 1e-7, separately from retrieval quality.
The implementation keeps the advanced path optional.
Existing collection backends retain their normal behav-
ior when it is disabled; older cache-statistic fields are
optional. Legacy plaintext databases do not become en-
crypted merely by reading them through a new interface:
2

==== Page 3 ====
migration to the vault-backed collection path is explicit.
2.1 Self-contained directory backend
A directory-backed collection places its database under
a reserved .rag-collection child of the selected root (Fig-
ure 2). This is a documented application format, not
a claim of OCFL, RO-Crate, BagIt or database-format
conformance. Its bootstrap identifies the persistent col-
lection UUID and storage mode. The default encrypted
mode includes a KDF and passphrase-wrapped ran-
dom master key; the optional cipher:none mode has an
integrity:sha256-v1 marker and no key or KDF. Hashed
logical-record names locate values, asset headers, aliases
and chunks. The local catalog holds binding identity,
policy and provider mapping, not vector or asset-header
copies. Existing central encrypted and read-only linked-
source routes remain compatible. Source manifests val-
idate bounded paths/counts, duplicate IDs/paths and
alias-to-file identity before use.
The single-writer protocol writes an immutable object,
reads it back, then exclusively creates and reads back a
commit marker binding digest, sequence and parent. In
encrypted mode, AEAD also authenticates the payload;
in clear mode, a checksum detects accidental damage
but is not a defense against a writer who can replace
records and markers. Derived manifests remain the
publication boundary; independent keys do not form
a distributed transaction. Conflicting per-key heads fail
closed. Cleanup removes oldest markers first and stops
at a deletion failure, retaining payloads while markers
could remain. Reads and enumeration share bounded
retry when cleanup removes a captured head; unchanged-
head corruption remains an error. Read-back establishes
completion, not filesystem flush durability or cross-device
exclusion.
Each newly published portable vector generation stores
the full portable model descriptor and its canonical-
contract SHA-256, alongside its original local space
binding. The descriptor covers provider type, sani-
tized endpoint, exact model/revision, requested dimen-
sions, transport, metric/normalization and separate
query/document prefix or task settings. The local reader
verifies descriptor/hash agreement and compatible local
mapping before rebinding provider identifiers. An in-
dependently updated descriptive configuration cannot
authorize incompatible vectors if that update fails. Cre-
dentials and endpoint/model consent remain local. Equal
vector dimension alone never establishes compatibility;
mutable remote model aliases without declared revisions
remain a limitation.
3
Document routing and model
responsibilities
3.1
Explicit representations and source
enrichment
Ingestion stores an immutable original, binds its verified
byte hash in the source manifest and publishes one man-
ifest for a bulk-upload batch. These records follow the
selected storage envelope. Parsing produces text with
source locations, or native media if a compatible adapter
genuinely accepts that modality. Legacy native-media
selection retains precedence over OCR/STT in the vector
route, preventing an upgrade from silently adding model
calls or a second representation. Advanced metadata
extraction can separately authorize text derivation from
native media. New opt-ins for visual descriptions or
file metadata can append text passages beside a native
vector; native embedding alone does not imply OCR,
transcription or description.
The PDF parser preserves existing page text and sends
only missing-text page images to an enabled OCR route.
An additional description option inspects every rendered
page, retaining existing text while adding an explicitly
inferred visual account. For images, the vision call can
return separate OCR text and a short description in
schema-validated JSON. OCR requests faithful reading
order; descriptions may summarize diagrams, charts and
objects but are labelled as model inference. STT uses
its separately selected model. No derivation call receives
agent tools or web search. Retained text is source- and
policy-bound; ordinary Markdown retention is optional.
Opening a citation uses retained text or a local parser
and never silently starts paid derivation
Optional local enrichment reads bounded JPEG
EXIF fields, recognized PNG text fields and selected
PDF properties, then retains filenames, paths and
MIME/size information as file-provided metadata. Lo-
cation/GPS has a separate opt-in. These values are
not authenticated identities or source facts. Recognized
EXIF/XMP/IPTC/comment and PNG text/EXIF meta-
data are removed before image upload to vision or native
embedding; JPEG orientation is retained for correct dis-
play. This reduces incidental metadata disclosure, not
information visible in the pixels. Indexing the extracted
fields can still intentionally send them as text to the
selected embedder/extractor.
3.2 Passage and analysis units
The recursive splitter targets 1,200 characters with 150
characters of overlap. It prefers section, paragraph and
line boundaries before word boundaries, and retains
line/page information. This inherited operating point is
a configuration choice, not a measured optimum. Passage
overlap serves local retrieval context; analysis windows
serve extraction, with a separate default budget of 8,000
characters. Their hashes and invalidation rules are there-
fore independent.
The extractor returns validated JSON containing a
short summary, open-domain entity types, directed sub-
ject/predicate/object relations and key/value tags. Ev-
ery entity, relation and tag carries a verbatim source
quote. Entity names must occur in their quote; re-
lation endpoints must be declared entities and both
names must occur in the retained relation span. Unsup-
ported relations are omitted individually with diagnos-
tics, rather than accepted or allowed to discard unrelated
valid records. These rules establish inspectable anchors;
semantic entailment remains a later assessment.

independent stores and passphrase-wrapped keys; ordinary originals remain outside encryption. The optional clear format uses
the same ownership layout without encryption or a portable key. Each vector generation embeds its compatibility contract;
metadata has its own extraction fingerprint. The registry holds local references/policy. Federation composes bounded ranks
and qualified graph records without copying vectors. Local access and optional provider consent remain separate: mounting
or graph viewing does not trigger inference.

3.3
Read-only linked-source snapshots
A read-only directory adapter connects a collection to
the desktop native picker or Android Storage Access
Framework. Collection authority is checked at the trans-
port boundary, and the native knowledge namespace
enforces read-only operations. The encrypted manifest
stores a binding token and display name; the platform
keeps the root mapping locally. A bounded scan hashes
actual bytes, stages changed encrypted source copies,
then swaps one source manifest before index refresh.
Missing, revoked, absent or incomplete list snapshots
preserve prior documents instead of becoming empty
deletion snapshots. Manual refresh is the default; an opt-
in 60-second foreground monitor pauses for background
visibility, locks or errors. Changed documents may incur
configured model calls. Grants are not restored from
backup.
This route imports snapshots rather than encrypting
an external live filesystem. External originals remain
outside the vault, and changes are known only after a
refresh observes them. Once a new managed source snap-
shot commits, old derivatives become ineligible through
revision checks. Scanning the external filesystem is not
atomic. Unchanged documents reuse vector and analysis
records, but a hash scan still incurs local file I/O; zero
model calls does not imply zero refresh work.

3.4
Managed desktop text recognition
An optional desktop OCR-role adapter routes attach-
ment recognition and per-collection/session OCR to an
owned local worker, outside the conversational model
catalog. The host validates the calling renderer, starts an
authenticated loopback service and supplies one image
with the fixed Text Recognition: prompt. Recognized
text rejoins the same source-bound derivative, chunking
and indexing contracts. It has no implicit cloud fall-
back. The adapter performs recognition only; it does
not include the upstream layout detector, region-specific
reconstruction pipeline or semantic image descriptions.
Their reported full-document performance cannot be
attributed to this narrower integration. [17
The installer accepts pinned Q4 or Q8 GGUF lan-
guage weights plus a required F16 vision projector, from
explicit download or verified local import. Artifact sizes
and SHA-256 are checked before activation; the infer-
ence runtime is pinned separately. CPU processing is
explicit; Vulkan offload requires device detection rather
than assuming GPU availability. Model artifacts belong
to the host installation, not a portable collection, and
document processing does not require a provider end-
point. Later embedding, extraction or verification can
still use independently configured remote models. [18]
Resource limits separate throughput from residency:
one recognition slot, bounded CPU threads, at most four
admitted jobs and 48 MiB of encoded input strings. This
input budget is not total RSS. Cancelling a queued job
returns promptly without interrupting the active page;
process stop and the next startup are serialized. A queue-
empty idle timer defaults to 120 seconds, with explicit
unload. PDF rendering prefetches at most one following
page. Memory-mapped weights are not a tiny guaran-
teed resident subset: inference also touches model layers,
the vision projector, context and temporary buffers. In-
tegrated GPUs share system RAM, and worker exit need
not discard the operating-system file cache. [18]
Algorithm 1. Incremental collection generation
check authority and cancellation

for each current source:
revision <- bound hash or SHA256(bytes)
if vector inputs/settings unchanged:
reuse prior vector records
else:
representation <- route(source, policy)
reuse exact compatible chunk hashes
embed unique missing inputs
stage vector shards and text refs
if metadata analysis enabled:
for each eligible text source:
reuse source/text/window hash matches
extract missing analysis windows
reanchor and validate retained quotes
stage source-owned analysis records
check authority and cancellation
publish derived pointer under write gate
remove unreferenced superseded records
4
Incremental indexing and gen-
eration publication
An ordinary update compares the source revision and
relevant configuration fingerprints before work is sched-
uled. Unchanged sources retain their vector shards and
metadata. Within a changed text document, the engine
hashes exact embedding inputs and reuses matching prior
vectors. It keeps hash-to-shard locations rather than a
second resident copy of every vector, loading required old
vectors in bounded shard reads. Duplicate new passages
in one batch are embedded once.
Metadata reuse is finer than whole-file invalidation.
Each extraction window stores a content hash. A match-
ing window reuses its entities, tags, summary and rela-
tions; if its position moved, anchor offsets shift and the
new parsed text must still equal the retained quote. If
raw container bytes change while parsed text remains
identical, metadata is rebound to the new raw revision
without an LLM call. Boundary changes can still affect
adjacent windows or passages; the algorithm reuses exact
inputs, not merely similar text.
Raw hashes bind immutable asset IDs at ingestion or
replacement. An operation-local manifest snapshot is
reused only while its immutable identity remains current.
The encrypted path avoids repeated full-source decryp-
tion during revision checks; legacy or changed aliases
fall back to actual-byte hashing. This discovers revisions
rather than continuously detecting bit rot: encrypted
reads authenticate ciphertext, while clear-format reads
check recorded digests.
Source uploads and replacements publish their as-
set/source manifest before the derived index is refreshed.
New vector, metadata and retained-text records are
then staged before a separate derived-generation pointer
changes. Readers use a publication/read gate for that
derived snapshot, while every returned passage must
still match the current source revision. A replacement
therefore makes old passages ineligible immediately; pre-
serving an older pointer does not preserve their trusted
status. Old derived records are removed after successful
publication. Cancellation or a pre-publication failure
5

==== Page 6 ====
Algorithm 2. Resumable collection migration
capture source signature and verified model binding
choose destination with a pending native grant
unlock/create portable bootstrap
reject foreign committed data or changed source
for each owned asset:
copy chunks; rewrap keys only for encrypted target
read back and verify the copied stream
publish generation contract and complete configuration
attach local catalog as cleanup-pending
adopt native grant and retire old app-owned assets
mark cleanup complete
on restart: resume only the matching source signature
leaves the previous pointer intact. If a storage adapter
reports failure after a pointer write may have committed,
recovery rereads it and removes only unreferenced assets;
unreadable state causes conservative retention.
Deletion removes the source's vector references, meta-
data, retained derivatives and citation receipts without
recomputing unrelated documents. Replacement pre-
serves the stable file identity, while old receipts remain
tied to their earlier source hash and appear historical.
Explicit Rebuild deliberately bypasses caches; routine
Update does not. Configuration fingerprints conserva-
tively invalidate compatible caches. Because the vector
fingerprint includes collection-level OCR/STT and model
settings, a configuration change may rebuild all collec-
tion vectors, even if only some source types need the
changed route. Routine source edits remain incremental
at document, chunk and analysis-window levels.
4.1
Moving storage without new infer-
ence
Migration copies assets individually without new em-
bedding or extraction calls. An encrypted destination
rewraps data keys under its portable master, preserving
physical asset UUIDs and authenticated alias strings;
a clear destination decrypts and writes checksummed
public chunks. Logical alias lookup maps the originat-
ing numeric collection prefix to the current mount. A
pending native grant leaves the source binding usable
until adoption. A source-signature bootstrap permits
resumption of the same revision and may initialize only
when no committed record, including a tombstone, exists.
Ambiguous staged objects are retained.
Registry publication, grant adoption and central-copy
retirement are separate recoverable phases. A cleanup-
pending record lets reopening finish after interruption;
failure before attachment abandons the pending grant.
A reliable external transfer copies a quiescent committed
directory. It is not a snapshot of a running writer or
garbage collector. The reference reader opens the copied
package without the originating application catalog or
device key and never loads providers or starts inference.

5.1 One exact scan, two retrieval lanes
The semantic lane compares normalized vectors inside
the selected collection's space. The lexical lane tokenizes
passage text and file-relative paths with Unicode normal-
ization, retaining identifiers and also splitting filename
separators. This makes named files retrievable even when
a native-media passage has no text; path tokens describe
the file, not unseen image/audio contents. BM25 docu-
ment frequencies and average length are calculated across
the scan, not estimated from a semantic shortlist.
The implementation collects lexical statistics during
the existing vector-shard scan instead of maintaining
a second plaintext inverted database. Vectors reside
one shard at a time; a small semantic shortlist and
query-matching lexical statistics survive the scan. This
favors simple storage protection and update ownership
over low query I/O. The initial search remains linear in
the number and dimension of vectors; lexical candidate
metadata can also grow with the number of matching
passages.

5.2 Optional reranking
A collection may select either a reranking API or a text
LLM through the same ordering contract. The virtual
reranker sees only the bounded query/candidate request,
with no conversation history, tools or web access. Strict
JSON validation rejects foreign indices, duplicates and
non-finite scores; omitted candidates retain their relative
order below explicitly ranked candidates. This is a single
listwise stage, not one model call per corpus document.
Native media without derived text preserves its original
retrieval order instead of pretending that an LLM has
seen the media.
5.3 Federation without vector-space
mixing
A conversation may attach up to eight collections. Pro-
tected collections authenticate sequentially to avoid com-
peting unlock prompts; retrieval then runs in bounded

index, access scope and reranking policy. The coordina-
tor fuses collection-local ranks with lexical evidence over
returned candidates, never comparing raw vectors or
uncalibrated cosine scores from different models. Results
retain collection/file identities and citation links.
Federation composes access and ranking, not storage.
It does not concatenate incompatible vectors into a new
index or copy every source into a global database. The
cost is per-collection query encoding and fan-out. Open-
domain metadata remains collection-scoped, so a multi-
collection agent first chooses a source collection when
expanding entities or reading a document.
5.4 Directory and graph federation
The explicit mounted-collection union supports up to 256
selected collections, with at most two executing concur-
rently. Each operation combines bounded per-collection
ranks rather than building a merged vector database.
A request-local promise cache reuses an identical query
embedding only for the same validated embedding-space
contract and exact input. It does not retain a cross-
session query cache. Owner-key revisions and mount
epochs are captured for every origin and rechecked
through the final federated return, so lock followed by
reopening the same root invalidates results begun before
revocation.
Graph federation qualifies local entity IDs by per-
sistent collection UUID; central-only collections use a
local namespace. Edges retain collection/file identity,
source/text revision and quotation anchors. Equal nor-
malized labels never establish cross-collection identity.
Duplicate UUID mounts are rejected rather than counted
as independent corroboration; divergent copies have no
automatic reconciliation. Bounded metadata pages com-
pose an inspection view without a central graph mirror,
global entity resolution or corpus-complete inference. Un-
mount removes the local grant/registration while leaving
the folder's data intact.

Agents receive small, explicit capabilities rather than
filesystem or database access. The base contract sup-
ports search, paginated file enumeration and consecutive
passage reads. The advanced contract adds metadata
discovery and exact source expansion. Metadata queries
can first discover source-language types and keys, then
filter by type, key or entity identity. Their query field is
an exact-token prefilter; semantic retrieval remains a sep-
arate operation. Android Work tool assembly registers
the same authorized global-collection/federation tools
on initial and resumed execution; engine portability and
harness registration are tested separately.
For a question such as “Which projects belong to this
client?", an agent can search for terminology, inspect
discovered entity types, paginate metadata to find con-
nected project records, and resolve their anchors through
knowledge_sources. It can read adjacent passages to
determine dates or scope before drafting. An exhaustive-
list request must traverse the applicable pages rather
than promote top-K similarity into a completeness claim.
The graph explorer offers the same bounded navigation
visually, with at most 150 nodes and 300 edges, deter-
ministic layout, pan/zoom and a touch-friendly relation
list.
For automatic review, the host builds a segment-local
ledger from completed recognized search, read, source
and intermediate-review tool results. It resolves real
KB receipts only from attached authorized collections
and accepts actual returned web URLs with bounded
snippets. An explicit intermediate knowledge_verify call
is available in Work chat only when a per-chat verifier is
enabled and consented; owner authentication and canon-

redundant checking before an automatically reviewed
final answer. Its returned receipt references can feed the
final ledger. KB revisions are rechecked around review
calls, while external snippets are snapshots, not live val-

legacy KB output without usable receipts may remain
unverified.
Citations resolve to collection-scoped evidence receipts
rather than to a free-form path. A receipt binds collec-
tion/file identity, source hash, exact quotation, adjacent
context and available line/page or text offsets. Opening
the reference authenticates its owner, rechecks access
after awaited work, highlights the retained excerpt and
offers the matching parsed document or supported native
viewer. If the source changed, the receipt remains visibly
historical instead of silently displaying replacement text.
A desktop MCP endpoint has an independent collec-
tion allowlist and cannot expand access by supplying
another session ID. Reading, mutation and model-call
permissions remain distinct. An authorized conversation
helper applies the same source-review boundary to its
nonstreaming reply, with additional knowledge/model
grants and approval for the verifier. The separately ex-
posed knowledge_verify tool remains an explicit route.
Externally spawned workers refuse implicit review; auto-
matic review is not claimed for every worker or auxiliary
model call.

8
Protection and operational life-
cycle
The default vault path encrypts managed source copies,
derivatives, vector shards, analysis and receipts under
collection access scopes. Per-asset keys are wrapped
by scope keys; AES-GCM authentication and associated
data bind assets/chunks to context. PIN or biometric un-
lock controls device access. The explicitly clear directory
path has neither confidentiality nor keyed authentication.
Linked-source directories do not encrypt external origi-
nals; protection applies to managed copies according to
their storage mode. Authorized excerpts copied into a
chat follow that conversation's lifecycle. [14]
Every storage/model port checks authority before work
and after awaited calls. Operations capture owner-key re-
vision and mount epoch, so even a rapid app lock/unlock
invalidates old work. Provider-setting changes also can-
cel affected operations. Indexing yields cooperatively
between bounded batches and extraction windows. Plain-
text source buffers are cleared after use; the system does
not retain a second in-memory copy of all corpus vectors.
The host still holds authorized plaintext while processing
it, so endpoint compromise remains outside the vault's
protection.
Remote models receive the data required by their
specific role: embedding inputs and queries, extraction
windows, reranking candidates, or draft/evidence pairs.
Local storage encryption does not conceal these from a
remote model endpoint. Model choice and consent are
therefore independent per stage. Similarly, an autho-
rized external MCP client receives plaintext results; its
subsequent retention is not controlled by the local vault.
Cleanup is ownership-based. Removing a source re-
moves its derived records, while generation reconciliation
preserves assets still referenced after ambiguous failures.
The central-library backup route validates identities and
scopes, creates fresh local collection identities, and re-
stores source assets before a consented index rebuild.
Portable directory copying instead retains its collection
UUID and committed indices. It does not silently restore
provider consent or operating-system directory grants.
8.1 Portable key and mount lifecycle
Encrypted portable records use a random 256-bit collec-
tion master independent of a device key. A passphrase-
derived AES-256-GCM key wraps that master using
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with a 128-bit random salt
and 600,000 iterations; record encryption uses 96-bit
nonces and 128-bit authentication tags. PBKDF2 pa-
rameterization is a versioned implementation choice, not
a password-strength guarantee. Local PIN/app autho-
rization is an additional device policy; it is not transferred
o

==== Page 10 ====
as the package password. A recipient must supply the
collection passphrase and grant local access. [15] [14]
In encrypted mode, the reserved directory protects
managed source copies, indices and retained derivatives.
Ordinary originals elsewhere in the chosen root remain
outside that encryption boundary. Shared-passphrase
holders can read the package; changing a local lock
cannot revoke copies or plaintext already retained by
a recipient. Authenticated encryption does not prove
publisher identity or that a copied generation is the lat-
est. Unmounting cancels active work and drops live key
access; persistent rollback detection, distributed writers
and recipient key revocation require additional protocols.
The optional clear format stores plaintext immutable
JSON values and public base64-encoded chunks with
SHA-256 checksums, without a collection master key.
Base64 is an encoding, not encryption. Opening an exist-
ing root detects its mode before requesting a passphrase.
Local PIN/app policy can restrict this application's ac-
cess but cannot protect a copied clear directory. Check-
sums may detect corruption relative to their recorded
manifest; an adversary able to rewrite that manifest
can recompute them. The mode must therefore not
be described as cryptographically authenticated public
distribution.
Deletion keeps a null tombstone and prunes super-
seded payloads. Exclusive-gate maintenance removes
orphan chunks/uncommitted objects after writes stop.
Logical cleanup cannot guarantee forensic erasure on
flash, replicas or backups.

A deterministic fixture exercised 1,000 short Markdown
documents, one passage per document, at 1,024 and 4,096

single fixed-order observations on a shared runner are

10
Limits and implementation
outlook
The exact vector/BM25 scan has O(Nd) vector work
for N passages of dimension d, plus tokenization, au-
thenticated storage reads and candidate bookkeeping.
Current guards allow 10,000 sources, 100,000 passages
and 10 MiB per source; these are operational limits
rather than measured quality/performance guarantees at
that scale. Vector dimensionality, legacy numeric-array
records and authenticated asset overhead can dominate
storage; packed new writes address representation cost.
Persistent authenticated lexical postings or a local ANN
index are possible next steps, with additional invalidation
and access-control complexity.
Relational extraction is open-world and model-
dependent. Canonical type/name hashes are useful navi-
gation identities, not full entity resolution; two organiza-
tions with the same name can still be conflated. Quotes
constrain provenance but do not prove entailment. The
graph remains deliberately bounded and non-exhaustive.
Likewise, an unchanged remote model alias cannot reveal
silently changed weights without a declared revision.
Generalized verifier accuracy, long-document and
visual-description quality, physical-device behavior and
clear-format adversarial provenance remain open evalua-
tion targets. Directive filtering recognizes only bounded
explicit patterns; obfuscated or semantically indirect
attacks can evade it, and legitimate discussion of instruc-
tions can be over-filtered. The source judge remains
fallible. Managed local inference is restricted to the
desktop OCR role; general-purpose local LLM runtimes
still require a separately configured compatible endpoint.
OCR transcription quality, reading order and resident-
memory use require direct measurement for the selected
quantization and backend. Further worker/auxiliary re-
view needs explicit integration.
